ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Read from the text of the problem: the solution set of the inequality ax^2-x+b≥0 is the closed interval [-2,1]. Therefore the two zeros of the quadratic function ax^2-x+b are -2 and 1, and because the solution set of ≥0 is between the two roots, the parabola opens downward. Let ax^2-x+b=k(x+2)(x-1). Expanding gives k(x+2)(x-1)=kx^2+kx-2k. Comparing with ax^2-x+b, the coefficient of the x term satisfies k=-1, so a=k=-1, b=-2k=2. Substituting a=-1 and b=2 into the inequality to be found bx^2-x+a≤0 gives 2x^2-x-1≤0. Factoring: 2x^2-x-1=(2x+1)(x-1), so (2x+1)(x-1)≤0. The two roots are x=-1/2 and x=1, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is positive, therefore the solution set of the inequality is the closed interval between the two roots, namely [-1/2,1].
